title: Altair mark_geo chart not rendered
body:
### Summary
Altair mark_geo chart not rendered

### Steps to reproduce


Code snippet:

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-2910)

```
import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data

states = alt.topo_feature(data.us_10m.url, 'states')
pop = data.population_engineers_hurricanes()

alt.Chart(states).mark_geoshape().encode(
	color='population:Q'
).transform_lookup(
	lookup='id',
	from_=alt.LookupData(pop, 'id', list(pop.columns))
).properties(
	width=500,
	height=300
).project(
	type='albersUsa'
)

```


**Expected behavior:**
works fine with altair
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43062719/110243821-fd836200-7f96-11eb-85ac-e323b3c02432.png)

**Actual behavior:**
when i do st.write(chart), i get an empty graph
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43062719/110243912-679c0700-7f97-11eb-8e5e-47df763303e4.png)


### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.62.1
- Python version: 3.7.8
- Using Pyenv
- OS version: macos 10.15.7
- Browser version: chrome & safari both failed

### Additional information

If needed, add any other context about the problem here. For example, did this bug come from https://discuss.streamlit.io or another site? Link the original source here!

comments.body: it seems that transform_lookup is what causes this error, when i removed it the graph could be rendered

### Triage summary

This is a confirmed bug: Altair `mark_geoshape()` charts render as an empty plot in Streamlit even though they display correctly in native Altair. The community discussion narrows it down to how Streamlit handles chart data: inline GeoJSON/TopoJSON geometry (and, as the reporter noticed, data pulled in via `transform_lookup`) gets dropped, so the shapes have nothing to draw.

**Likely root cause:** When converting an Altair chart to a Vega-Lite spec, Streamlit installs a custom data transformer (`_to_arrow_dataset` in `lib/streamlit/elements/vega_charts.py`) that serializes every inline dataset to Arrow IPC bytes via `convert_anything_to_arrow_bytes()`. Geometry / nested GeoJSON structures don't round-trip through a tabular Arrow/DataFrame representation — the geometry (`coordinates`, `features`, etc.) is flattened or lost during serialization — so `mark_geoshape` ends up with no geometry to render. This matches the observation that a chart defined purely by a remote data URL renders, while inline/GeoPandas geometry does not.

### Related Issues

- [#1002 - Add support for geometry dtype in `st.altair_chart`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1002) — Directly linked in this thread; same underlying limitation that geometry data types aren't supported by Streamlit's Arrow-based chart data serialization.
- [#6099 - `st.altair_chart` removes data from a compound plot with interaction that works with `altair`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6099) — Same class of bug where data is dropped for charts with transforms/interactions, consistent with the reporter finding that `transform_lookup` triggers the empty render.
- [#6269 - `st.altair_chart` unable to display alt.Chart that is deserialized from json](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6269) — Another case where a valid Altair spec renders as a blank chart due to how Streamlit marshals the chart data.
